The supertrend with a multiplier of 3 may lag on 5‑min data, causing missed entries and whipsaw exits; the ADX >25 filter is very restrictive, cutting out many profitable moves. 2. If the backtest shows negative returns, I would lower the ADX threshold to 20 or 15 and reduce the supertrend multiplier to 2.0 to capture more entries and avoid over‑filtering. 3. For a mediocre Sharpe, tightening the stop to 1.5×ATR and reducing the TP to 4×ATR would improve risk‑reward; alternatively, extend the ATR period to 20 to smooth volatility. 4. If the strategy fails overall, I would switch to a trend‑following EMA crossover (e.g., 20‑EMA vs 50‑EMA) with an ATR‑based trailing stop, or implement a breakout filter (e.g., daily high/low) to capture stronger moves.
